statement: Wind Walker is the Beastmaster masterclass with an overhauled kit and an efficient respawn mechanic. Its core gameplay loop is demanding.
Wind Walker comes with a new core class tree.
Wind Walker has tons of summons while farming a ton of dust.
Outfit and artwork look like the Emerald Dream; he says it doesn't look like a ghillie suit.
He maxed everything with 400 talents when he got Wind Walker and pre-repped for a while so did not struggle.
The game mode revolves around Tempest mode. It requires pushing maps again like Deathbringer and slaying abominations.
Wind Walker is far more enjoyable than Death Bringer; same mechanic but flashier like Owl and Rue.
The talent tree is confusing and daunting for newcomers.
Run full drop rate gear for this build instead of Deathbringer's fishing gear.
Luck factor boosts the drop chance of all Tempest items by a percentage of your normal drop rarity.
His luck factor upgrade is 6% and he runs 110% drop rate, giving 654% Tempest drop rate.
Tempest mode drops new weapons rings and medallions that are only available in Tempest.
The ballista is completely overhauled and way better by a long shot; it's no longer active.
Commandments give longer duration (garbled) and more summons from your nachos and bors.
He wishes bear trap did an AoE explosion when stepped on.
Whale Wallup's cooldown was reduced; it was massively long before and now clearing feels possible.
Wind Walker is really good at Killroy but players never do their Killroys.
It takes him about 2 days to get level 15 shinies with nine shinies in each fence yard slot.
He was surprised he enjoyed abomination fighting as much as he did.
Gear progression gives bows and rings plus upgrade stones.
Upgrade stones come in 60% 30% or 10% chance types. Only use the 10% chance ones; 60% and 30% are a waste of time.
Wind Walker greatly boosts your sneaking.
Getting to Mastery? 4 (garbled) is very easy.
Elemental weakness system: monsters are weak to wind fire grass ice and even milk.
You must go through all the worlds and progress again like Deathbringer; a soft prestige system. He thinks that is the best way.
An upgrade gives monsters coliseum chests event mobs and mini bosses a chance to drop a medallion.
Medallions give a massive XP multiplier outside Tempest and a great amount of damage within Tempest.
Medallion farming is his favorite part and gave the same dopamine as old-school card farming with Elemental Sorcerer.
Upgrade stones are a double-edged sword. The 10% chance feels more like 1%.
An upgrade gives a 50% failsafe chance to not consume an upgrade stone but it barely helps.
Without the 50% failsafe a five out of five upgraded bow is about 1 in 100000 odds per ChatGPT.
Damage scaling is awful. When farming abominations with the deer summon Wind Walker doesn't hit the abomination and hits everything else.
A talent increases crit chance in Tempest based on breedability levels; he thinks it should be based on shinies.
Deathbringer bonuses felt stronger overall; you get 20 extra atom levels but many cost reduction talents feel like filler.
He asks Lava to add an upgrade giving a higher chance at upgrading stones.
A huge chunk of the tree is accuracy but you only need about three nodes for enough accuracy for world 7.
Eternal Hunt says it spawns a reindeer whose death brings life; this isn't just flavor text and it is functional.
Weapon improvement says Tempest weapons drop with higher power based on mob HP but it's actually based on the world. Each world has a weapon power cap.
He has been in Wind Walker for a week and will make a full guide once the dust settles.
You need two setups: a dust farming setup and an abomination farming setup.
For dust use one dust ring, one elemental ring matching the mob's weakness, and a dust bow, since elemental is a separate multiplier.
Later you won't have damage for double dust rings. Farm a 3 out of 3 elemental ring of each type for a one and done; then farm bows.
Against abominations use the elemental bows the boss is weak to and two Tempest power rings that drop from purple mushrooms.
Top of the Morning upgrade increases medallion drop chance 200 times for a limited number of mobs per daily reset; works with golden stopwatches.
Before daily reset clear a coliseum without opening chests; after reset open the chests to get the boosted medallion chance.
Run mini bosses like Biggy Hours and Glanco during Top of the Morning since their medallions are huge.
You can't spot crystal mobs in Tempest mode so use the Glitterbug prayer for crystal mob medallions.
Glitterbug spawns crystals when killing giants; use chocolate chip to potentially respawn them.
After weekly reset with Top of the Morning equip Glitterbug and another prayer (garbled) and farm one mob at a time until a giant spawns; kill it to trigger crystals.
Getting the final-area medallion (garbled name) gives a massive XP multiplier and gets you close to level 900.
When farming abominations take off the Urar? and Eternal Hunt talents so mobs stop spawning and Wind Walker focuses the abomination; boss farming becomes three times faster.
Wind Walker is incredibly fun and a main for now but he wouldn't get two of them.
Don't buy the Spirit Reindeer pack unless your arcade is juiced; it's strong on paper only if already deep into the upgrades.
The pack is bad if you've never done events and lack cosmic balls; it's for whales and other packs are better.
Wind Walker is now a much better shiny and breedability farmer and makes sneaking much easier.
Wind Walker is very active so AFK players might wait for an AFK dust update.
Class is for sweaty grinders willing to reroll rings and weapons for hours to get a good one.
He is currently in world five of the Wind Walker progression.
He gives Wind Walker 9 out of 10 but still ranks it below Divine Knight.
